Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:47506
Court No. - 76

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 54740 of 2023
Applicant :- Ankit Kumar

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Syed Faiz Hasnain,Syed Riyaz Askari
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Jagdish Prasad Mishra
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Syed Faiz Hasnain, learned counsel for the applicant; Sri Abhilash Singh Advocate holding brief of Sri Jagdish Prasad Mishra, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Imran Khan,
learned AGA for the State-respondent.

3. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
423 of 2023, under Sections 328, 376(D) IPC, Police Station Budhana, District Muzaffar Nagar,
during pendency of the trial in the court below.
4.

entities.text: Police Station Budhana, District Muzaffar Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: FIR of the present case was lodged on 17.09.2023 against applicant and his one unknown associate and according to the FIR, on 16.09.2023 at about 10:00 a.m. in the morning applicant by playing fraud, provided cold drink to the wife of the informant and after that when she fainted then he has taken her to the forest and thereafter called his three unknown friends and all the accused persons committed gang rape upon her.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that on the basis of false allegation applicant has been made accused in the present matter and he never committed rape upon the victim alongwith others as alleged by the prosecution.
6. He further submitted that even story narrated by the victim appears to be improbable and no reliance can be placed on such version.

7. He further submitted that admittedly victim is a married lady, she is the wife of the informant and no reliance can be placed on her statements recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
8.

He further submitted that as per allegation applicant alongwith three others committed rape upon the victim but surprisingly doctor did not note even a single scratch on her body and this fact clearly suggests that on the basis of false allegation of gang rape, applicant has been made accused in the present matter alongwith others.

9. He further submitted that however, medical report of the victim suggests that she was having stomach pain but merely on the basis of pain in stomach/abdomen, it cannot be said that rape was committed against her.
10.

He further submitted the bail applications of two co-accused Riyasat and Jitendra has been allowed by this Court, however, both the accused were not named in the FIR but as far as allegation of rape is concerned, the allegation of rape was also against them.

11. He further submitted that however applicant is having criminal history of six other cases but his criminal history has been explained in para-3 of the supplementary affidavit and out of six cases,
one is of the provisions of gangster Act and one case is of Section 380, 511 IPC and one case is of under sections 102, 41 Cr.P.C.
12.
He further submitted that in all the cases applicant is on bail and all the cases are of the year 2016.
13. He further submitted that applicant is in jail in the present matter since 19.9.2023.

14. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that it is a case of gang rape and as per allegation applicant alongwith three others committed rape upon the victim and he was named in the FIR but they could not dispute the fact that no external or internal injury was found by the doctor upon the body of the victim and victim is a married lady.
15. They further could not dispute the fact that two accused persons have been released on bail by this Court.
16. I have heard learned counsel for both the sides and perused the record of the case.

sentences.text: However, applicant is named in the FIR and as per allegation, he provided some intoxicated drink to the victim and thereafter has taken her to the field and committed rape upon her alongwith his three associates but this Court finds forced in the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that the story narrated by the victim does not appear to be convincing.
18. Further, victim is a married lady and during her medical examination, doctor did not find any external or internal injury on her body.

19. Further, two co-accused persons (however they were not named in the FIR) have already been released on bail and their names, were disclosed by the victim in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C, therefore, there was allegation of rape against them too.

20. Further, however applicant is having criminal history of six other cases but his criminal history has been explained in the supplementary affidavit and it appears that out of six cases, one case is of theft and one case relates to the provisions of gangsters Act and one case was under the provision of Cr.P.C. and remaining three cases were of sections 307, 392 IPC and Arms Act and in all the cases applicant is on bail and all these cases were of the year 2016 and since 2016 to 2023 i.e. till the date of incident, no case has been lodged against the applicant.
21. Further, applicant is in jail in the present matter since September, 2023.

22. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
23. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

24. Let the applicant-Ankit Kumar, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
25. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
